title: Draft: TCP: Have overriding of SEQ analysis be done on marked packets
description:
Rather than muddy the waters with the GUI notion of "selected packets", use the frame_data information of "marked packets" to determine if the TCP preference "default_override_analysis" should be applied.

This greatly simplifies how the preference can be more generically handled and the custom code for the preference has been removed.

notes.body: I like the change architecturally, but it is a slight change in what the user has to do.  Where should I document that (since I don't see the original feature explicitly documented)?

So this does make it impossible to change some packets to one interpretation and other packets to a different interpretation, right? All the marked packets have to be the same?

I agree that the current implementation is a hack architecturally, but this does seem to be a decrease in functionality.

And maybe I'm not fully understanding the previous implementation.  Are the "selected packets" _permanently_ changed, so you can make i.e. packets 10-12 one type and packets 100-102 another type?  The goal was really just to replace "selected packets" with "marked packets" because that's cleaner architecturally.

Yes, they are *permamently* changed (for a certain value of "permanent" - it's not saved in the file if you close and reopen it; I'm not sure without checking whether it holds if the file is redissected by changing another preference but I think it does.) and some packets can be changed to Retransmission while others are changed to Out of Order.
It's in the prefs menu, so it ends up writing it to a "preference value" that is stored in memory (but never written to disk). It's quite odd to me architecturally.
